title: An introduction the founder answered only to the introducer

objects.subject: Intro: Arjun (Nimbus Labs) <> Tarun (Quillstack)
objects.body:
Hi Arjun, Tarun,

Connecting you two as promised. Tarun leads partnerships at Quillstack and is looking for workflow tools for their founder community; Arjun runs Nimbus Labs. I'll let you two take it from here.

Mira

objects.subject: Re: Intro: Arjun (Nimbus Labs) <> Tarun (Quillstack)
objects.body:
Thanks Mira, appreciate the intro!

Arjun

expected.workstream: intro - Tarun never heard from you; your reply went only to Mira

not_expressible.workstream: the file exists since STEP-09, but no line compares who an answer reached with who was introduced

facts.claim: Mira Kapoor introduced Arjun and Tarun in one mail to both of them, saying Tarun leads partnerships at Quillstack and is looking for workflow tools for its founder community.
facts.quote: Tarun leads partnerships at Quillstack and is looking for workflow tools for their founder

facts.claim: Mira handed the conversation over in the same mail: she would let the two of them take it from there.
facts.quote: let you two take it from here. Mira

facts.claim: The introduction is the file's only touch: no answer from Arjun to Tarun is measured, and the dossier says we have not written in this file.
The file holds nothing from Tarun himself either; his reply time is not measured.
The file has been quiet for about two weeks since the introduction, and the dossier names no stop rule for it.
The engine holds the file as an admin account and records it as seen for the first time.

inferences.claim: Tarun has had no word from Arjun since Mira handed the introduction to them: the move she left to both of them has not been made from our side.
Quillstack is more than a contact: a partnerships lead looking for workflow tools for a founder community is close to the brief's goal of landing design partners.
Every further week of quiet makes the first note weaker and leaves Mira's introduction looking ignored on our side.

hypotheses.proposition: Arjun answered the introduction where this file cannot see it: a call, a chat, or a mail on another thread.
hypotheses.needs: Arjun's word; the file shows no mail from us to Tarun.

hypotheses.proposition: Tarun is waiting for Arjun to write first, since Mira introduced Arjun as the one with something to offer Quillstack's founder community.
hypotheses.needs: A first note from Arjun, and whether Tarun answers it.

unknowns.question: Whether Arjun has reached Tarun outside this mailbox.
unknowns.relevance: If he has, nothing is owed; if not, the introduction has gone unanswered on our side for about two weeks.

unknowns.question: What Tarun wants for Quillstack's founder community: a tool to use, to recommend, or to build on together.
unknowns.relevance: It sets what the first note offers, and whether this becomes partner work or a sale.

frames.primary: An introduction left unanswered on our side: about two weeks ago Mira put you in touch with Tarun, who leads partnerships at Quillstack and wants workflow tools for its founder community, and the file shows no word from you to Tarun since.
rivals: The conversation moved off this thread, to a call or a direct mail the file does not see, and nothing is missing.
Tarun's interest was more Mira's framing than his own, and a note would land cold whenever it went.

proposed_kind.why: The file is an introduction in motion: a connector put Tarun and Arjun in touch and left it to them to take forward, and the brief names no kind of work for it. Proposed for the founder to accept.

expected_vs_actual.expected: Without a playbook, Mira's own words set it: she handed the introduction to the two of them, so each was to write to the other, and Arjun, who has what Tarun is looking for, first.
expected_vs_actual.actual: About two weeks on, the file holds only Mira's introduction: no mail from Arjun to Tarun, and nothing from Tarun.

scenarios.do_nothing: The introduction goes cold: Tarun reads the silence as no interest, Quillstack's founder community stays out of reach, and Mira's goodwill is spent for nothing.
scenarios.act: A short direct note to Tarun now revives it while Mira's introduction is still recent enough to mention, and puts a call on the table.
scenarios.best: Tarun answers, a call follows, and Quillstack becomes a way into its founder community, perhaps a design partner.
scenarios.worst: Tarun has moved on and the note goes unanswered, and Mira hears that her introduction was left hanging on our side.
signals_to_watch: A call with Quillstack on the calendar
Mira asking how it went with Tarun
No word from Tarun a week after Arjun writes

reasons: Quillstack's partnerships lead is looking for workflow tools for a founder community, close to the brief's goal of landing design partners.
The introduction is about two weeks old and the file shows no word from us to Tarun.
A short note is cheap to send, and easy to follow with a call or to let rest.

next_move.what: Write to Tarun directly: a short note picking up Mira's introduction, saying what you do for founders, and proposing a call
next_move.for_whom: Tarun, who leads partnerships at Quillstack

answer.alternative: If Tarun does not answer within a week, send one short second note with a specific time for a call, then let it rest.
answer.wait_or_stop: Do not wait: the introduction is already about two weeks old. After Arjun writes, give Tarun about a week; after one unanswered nudge, stop and keep the file for a later reason to write.
answer.done_when: Tarun has heard from you directly, and either a call is set or Tarun has said where Quillstack stands.
answer.draft: Hi Tarun, picking up Mira's introduction, and sorry for the slow start on my side. I run Nimbus Labs; we are building an AI chief of staff for founders. Mira mentioned you are looking at workflow tools for Quillstack's founder community, and I would love to hear what you have in mind. Would a short call next week work? Arjun

facts.claim: Mira Kapoor wrote to Arjun and Tarun together to introduce them, as she had promised, said Tarun leads partnerships at Quillstack, and left the two of them to take it from there.
Arjun's one mail in the file is a short thank-you to Mira for the introduction; it says nothing to Tarun.
The thank-you went out the same day the introduction arrived.
The file has been quiet since the thank-you, longer than the one gap it closed before; the dossier says no reply since then may be said.
The engine holds Mira's file as an admin account seen for the first time, and the brief names no kind of work or role for it.

inferences.claim: Mira's part is done: she made the introduction, stepped back, and has been thanked; nothing in the file is owed to her, and her quiet is expected.
The work the introduction opened lies with Tarun: our one mail here speaks only to Mira, and whether it reached Tarun at all is not shown.
Mira acts as a connector for Arjun, though the brief's connectors name only Introly.

patterns.claim: Arjun answers Mira fast: the one gap the file closed was within the day, so slowness toward her is not the risk here.

hypotheses.proposition: The thank-you went to Mira alone, so Tarun has heard nothing from Arjun.
hypotheses.needs: The thank-you's recipients, or a look at what Tarun has received from Arjun.

hypotheses.proposition: Mira will ask how the conversation with Tarun went.

unknowns.question: Whether Arjun's thank-you copied Tarun.
unknowns.relevance: If not, the introduction is unanswered on the side that matters and the move lies with Tarun; this file still needs nothing.

unknowns.question: Whether Mira introduces people to Arjun often.
unknowns.relevance: If so, she belongs among the brief's connectors, so her mail reads as an introduction rather than an account to manage.

frames.primary: A connector's file whose work is done: Mira introduced you to Tarun of Quillstack, stepped back, and was thanked the same day; nothing here is owed to her, and what the introduction opened lies with Tarun.
rivals: An introduction left half-answered: the thank-you may be the only answer it got, so Tarun has heard nothing; a live risk, but one that lies with Tarun, not in Mira's file.
An account to manage, as the engine files it; nothing in the mail supports that.

expected_vs_actual.expected: Without a playbook, from Mira's own words: once she hands the introduction over and is thanked, her file goes quiet and the work moves to the introduced pair.
expected_vs_actual.actual: Mira introduced and stepped back, Arjun thanked her the same day, and the file has been quiet since, as it should be.

scenarios.do_nothing: Mira's file stays quiet, as it should; nothing is lost here. What doing nothing loses, it loses with Tarun, if he was never written to.
scenarios.act: Writing to Mira again adds nothing she asked for; the move that matters is a direct note to Tarun.
scenarios.best: Arjun and Tarun are talking, and Mira's introduction pays off without her having to step back in.
scenarios.worst: Tarun hears nothing, the introduction goes cold, and Mira learns it went unanswered on Tarun's side.
signals_to_watch: A mail from Tarun or anyone at Quillstack
Mira asking how it went with Tarun
Mira writing with a new introduction

reasons: Mira's note handed the introduction over and asked nothing more of Arjun.
Arjun has already thanked her for it.
The introduction's value lies with Tarun, outside this file.

answer.alternative: Make sure Tarun has heard from Arjun directly; that is the introduction's open move, and it lies with Tarun, not here.
answer.wait_or_stop: Nothing to wait for here: treat Mira's file as closed, and reopen it only if she writes again.
answer.done_when: Mira's introduction has become a direct conversation between you and Tarun, and her file needs nothing more.

notes: 09 G1, the benchmark's introducer shape: an introduction with the introduced person in To, and the founder's thanks went to the introducer alone - the introduced person was never written to. No promise in the thanks: a promise would be caught as an overdue promise (F49's shape), and this case holds the structural miss alone. The card is about Tarun, never the connector (F37's rule).
